newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK British governor denounces China troop move.
newsitem.headline: HK British governor denounces China troop move.

text.p: Outgoing Governor Chris Patten on Friday denounced Beijing's decision to send in 4,000 troops by land, sea and air just hours after this British colony is handed over to China on July 1.
"It doesn't sound to me the right sort of signal to send to the international community and above all I think it is a most appalling signal to send to the people of Hong Kong," he told reporters.

China plans to send 4,000 troops, backed by helicopters, ships and armoured cars into Hong Kong just six hours after the formal midnight (1600 GMT) handover ceremony which ends more than 150 years of British rule.
Patten said: "I do think that it is most unfortunate that this decision has been made. We will continue to make representation and hope that this decision is reversed.
"I think I'm right in saying the arrival of the armoured personnel carriers will more or less coincide with the evening network news in the United States of America."
The office of Hong Kong's new Chief Executive-designate, chosen by Beijing to replace Patten, announced China's plans to send in the large body of troops by land, sea and air.
